open_issues.text: Choices outside the contract: (1) with sha from the source part, sha/paths/paths_digest describe the source commit, otherwise the workspace commit (repo says which); (2) when no source commit exists and the workspace part is locked, failed or skipped-no-git, commit returns exit 0 with sha null and that status instead of raising (op_commit then answers COMMIT_RESULT_INVALID naming the workspace error); (3) git.lock wait is 10 s (module constant gitops.WORKSPACE_LOCK_TIMEOUT), shorter than the 60 s in the W7 text, per the item rules; (4) the workspace commit supplies a fallback git identity (skm-workspace) when none is configured, like the workspace module; (5) a path given to --path or in task_files is sent to the workspace when it is @plan/..., inside the plan directory, or starts with the plan prefix, otherwise to the source repo.

summary: plan.py commit for a plan in the workspace now makes two commits: product paths in the source repo (Plan.source_root), then plan files in the workspace repo under git.lock (10 s) with Plan-Project and Plan-Source-Commit. Foreign workspace paths stay out and never give OUTSIDE_SCOPE; a workspace failure after the source commit is status failed with exit 0; NOTHING_TO_COMMIT only when both parts are empty; a reviewer commits to the workspace only. Result gets repo, workspace_sha, workspace_commit (legacy: source, null, skipped-legacy), and workspace_paths and workspace_outside for workspace plans. commits reads the checkout history, with source_unbound true when no checkout is bound. op_commit passes the new fields on for workspace plans and names a failed workspace part in message; the legacy answer is unchanged. Old commit logic moved into _commit_part; _allowed split into _plan_patterns and product patterns, plus a router (_route) that sends each path to the right repo.
